To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high self-monitoring people are less likely to act on their attitudes because their attitudes are less accessible in memory.
low self-monitoring people are more likely to act on their attitudes, and that high self-monitoring people can be more easily influenced by others.
high -and low- self-monitoring individuals differ in terms of their self-concept accessibility and attitude accessibility, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of attitude accessibility in the self-monitoring -attitude-behavior relation.
the relation between selfmonitoring and attitude accessibility.
the question of how the self-monitoring personality variable influences the accessibility of attitudes from memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the self-monitoring concept is a useful and valid construct that has been used to explain a wide array of interesting and important findings.
self-monitoring is a complex and multifaceted construct.
self-monitoring moderates the relationship between attitude and behavior by influencing the accessibility of attitude information in memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high self-monitors are more sensitive to the social context and are more likely to adjust their attitudes and behavior in response to situational factors.
self-monitoring influences the attitude-behaviour relation by influencing accessibility of attitudes to memory.
high self-monitoring is associated with a more complex and less accessible set of attitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the attitudes of high-self monitoring individuals are more context-dependent than those of low self-monitorers.
the self-monitoring scale is a useful tool in predicting how individuals will respond to a wide range of stimuli, from advertisements to political candidates.
the attitudes of high -and low self-monitoring subjects can be differentiated by their accessibility from memory.
